messages:
jessica: paging — alert: sustained 4x baseline request rate to /v1/embeddings from ~20 distinct IP clusters, 99th p99 latency up and 502s climbing. looks like a scrape farm targeting public endpoints.

pagerduty: Incident assigned to jessica (oncall-sre). Priority: P1.

jessica: confirming. dashboards show traffic spike started 00:06 UTC. origins appear to be rotating proxies, UA strings are generic 'python-requests'.

tom: grabbing live netflow, will correlate with WAF logs. if it's a scraper we should throttle before WAF blocks to avoid collateral on real customers.

maya: have customer-facing impact been reported? any 5xx errors to users?

jessica: some customers are seeing degraded embedding throughput (queued requests), small # of 502s from overloaded backend queues. not widespread but growing.

leo: proposed live mitigations: 1) apply adaptive per-key throttles on embeddings route, 2) enable soft WAF challenge (HTTP 403->CAPTCHA) for offending IP groups, 3) enable circuit-breaker on batch endpoints to shed heavy batch requests.

jessica: agree. ordering: throttles first, then circuit-breaker, then WAF challenge if traffic persists. want to avoid breaking legitimate traffic.

tom: I'll push a rate-limit rule to edge (FastEdge) with dynamic token bucket: burst=200/min per API key, sustained=60/min. rule id: rl-1783-proactive. command: `edgectl apply-rule --id rl-1783 --route /v1/embeddings --per-key --burst 200 --sustained 60`.

leo: deploying now. small note: apply-rule rollout will take ~45s to propagate to all POPs.

incident-bot: edge-rule rl-1783 applied (commit: a9c3f). propagation status: 32/32 POPs online.

jessica: monitoring token usage and error rates. plotting per-key rejects.

maya: should we notify customers proactively that we're throttling to mitigate abusive traffic? recommend #incidents -> status page if any customer-visible limits changed.

jessica: yes. I'll draft a short status update after we stabilize.

tom: after throttles, I see per-key qps drop 3.2x from offending keys. overall p99 latency dropped 40%. good signal.

jessica: next step: enable circuit-breaker on batch ingestion (route /v1/embeddings:batch). rule: reject >10 concurrent batches per key, fallback 429. command: `orchestrator set-cb embeddings_batch --concurrency 10 --fallback 429`.

leo: cb applied. logs: 88 keys were tripped within first minute — mostly keys with >500 req/min historically.

jessica: flagging 88 keys for review. not all are malicious; some high-volume partners. we'll throttle but allow manual override for partners.

maya: list please. we need to notify partners/SEs so they can whitelist if needed.

jessica: exporting list: `cat /var/logs/cb-trips/1783000001.log | jq '.key'` — sending to #customer-success offline.

tom: traffic pattern: rotating IP prefixes with short lifetimes. WAF rule with challenge should catch the IP clusters if they persist. propose enabling soft challenge for /v1/embeddings filtered by suspicious UA + ASN set.

leo: enabling WAF challenge (mode: 'simulate->challenge') to start: `wafctl rule add --name scrape-farm-challenge --route /v1/embeddings --conditions 'ua contains python' or 'asn in [X,Y,Z]' --action challenge --mode simulate`.

incident-bot: waf rule 'scrape-farm-challenge' applied in simulate mode.

jessica: simulate for 10m, then switch to active if challenge pass rate >80% on offending traffic and <0.5% on known customer IPs.

tom: sim results after 8m: 94% of matched sessions come from flagged IPs, 0.1% overlap with partner IP ranges. safe to flip.

leo: flipping to active challenge now.

incident-bot: waf rule 'scrape-farm-challenge' mode set to active. challenge served to 1.1k sessions in last 2m.

jessica: excellent. combined throttles + cb + WAF challenge reduced abusive qps by ~85%. error noise fell and p99 latency back near baseline.

maya: customer impact check: which paid customers experienced >5% error rate increase?

jessica: two small customers (acct-925, acct-412) had transient 429s due to cb. both are non-critical low-volume customers. we will credit affected tokens and send notes.

maya: ok. escalate for any enterprise partner impacted. looks like none.

tom: follow-up: raised a config task to make per-key adaptive throttle more aggressive for unknown keys by default. ticket INF-4123.

leo: ops note: added temporary quota bump endpoint for partners to request whitelist overrides: `POST /internal/whitelist-override {key, until}` — guarded by SSO and audit log.

jessica: handing to next oncall (tom) in 15m. summary I'll include in runbook: detection (anomaly in qps), Mitigations (edge throttle, batch cb, WAF challenge), customer impact (2 small accounts, credited), follow-ups (INF-4123, whitelist endpoint), rollback plan (remove cb, remove rl-1783, disable WAF challenge).

jessica: anyone object to closing once tom confirms stability for 30m? :thumbsup:

tom: lgtm. I'll monitor for 30m and then close the incident.

incident-bot: Incident incident-1783000001 transitioned to monitoring.

jessica: drafting status page note now, will include short timeline and mitigations.

leo: saved firewall snapshots and logs to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1783000001/.

jessica: thanks team. after-monitoring follow-ups: runbook update to include heuristic for 'python-requests' UA and automated temporary throttle for keys with no contact email.

tom: noted. adding to INF-4123.

jessica: handing off — tom will close after monitoring window. thanks. :slightly_smiling_face:
